heading: PREVENTION, PROTECTION AND RECOVERY OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AS VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN INDRAMAYU REGENCY
translated_text:
PREVENTION, PROTECTION AND RECOVERY OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AS VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN INDRAMAYU REGENCY

REGIONAL GAZETTE

INDRAMAYU REGENCY

NUMBER: 18 YEAR 2012

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF INDRAMAYU REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Indramayu Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent together with Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Indramayu.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Indramayu Regency as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Agency is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit authorized in the field of Prevention, Protection and Recovery of Women and Children as Victims of Violence in Indramayu Regency.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb and marriage cannot change the status of a child.
8. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
9. Recovery is rehabilitating victims until they are physically and/or psychologically healthy and accepted by society again.
10. Protection is an activity and/or action in order to protect women and children from violence and exploitation.
11. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
12. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death.
13. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence, whether physical, psychological or sexual violence.
16. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
18. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
19. Institution is an agency/body and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe house (Shelter) is temporary housing, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. P2TP2A is a form of service facility for women and children in the effort to fulfill information and needs in the fields of education, health, economy, law, protection and prevention of acts of violence and trafficking against women and children.

heading: CHAPTER II
translated_text:
CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The implementation of Prevention, Protection and Recovery of Women and Children as Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of:
a. Respect for the rights of victims;
b. Gender justice and welfare;
c. Non-discrimination; and
d. Best interests of victims.

heading: Article 3
CHAPTER III
CHAPTER IV
CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

PREVENTION AND PROTECTION

Part One

Institutional

heading: Article 6
translated_text:
Article 6

1. In the framework of implementing prevention, protection and recovery for women and children victims of violence in an integrated, harmonious, and sustainable manner, the Regent establishes P2TP2A at the Regency level.
2. Further provisions regarding the establishment of P2TP2A management, P2TP2A membership, and P2TP2A working procedures as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Regent.
3. Regency P2TP2A may receive case referrals from Hospitals, Community Health Centers, NGOs, Safe Houses (Shelters) and the Community.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Forms and Mechanisms of Prevention

heading: Article 7
translated_text:
Article 7

Forms of prevention of acts of violence against women and children carried out by P2TP2A can be implemented through:
a. socialization activities of laws and regulations and/or regional regulations to the community related to the protection of the rights of women and children;
b. training of P2TP2A members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing acts of violence against women and children.

heading: Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

1. Regency P2TP2A in carrying out its duties and functions may coordinate with the Religion and Social Welfare Section of the Indramayu Regency Regional Secretariat, sub-districts and competent parties in making efforts to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
2. The mechanism for implementing prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 9
Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

1. In carrying out the task of serving victims of acts of violence against women and children, the Regency P2TP2A coordinates with the Sub-district Health Center.
2. The mechanism for implementing tasks as referred to in paragraph (1) is regulated in the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Assistance Mechanism

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

1. Assistance is carried out by persons and institutions cooperating with P2TP2A.
2. The assistance mechanism as referred to in paragraph (1) is set forth in the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).
3. Provisions regarding the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for the assistance mechanism as referred to in paragraph (2) are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Principles of Prevention, Protection and Recovery

heading: Article 12
CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

RECOVERY

Part One

Minimum Service Standards

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

1. In the context of implementing prevention, protection and recovery for women and children victims of acts of violence in an integrated, harmonious and sustainable manner, the Regional Government establishes Minimum Service Standards (SPM).
2. Further provisions regarding Minimum Service Standards as referred to in paragraph (1) are further regulated by Regent Regulation.
3. The Regional Government is obliged to apply Minimum Service Standards in Hospitals, Health Centers, NGOs, Safe Houses (Shelters) designated by the Regent.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Forms and Mechanisms of Recovery

heading: Article 14
CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE, CONTROL AND

SUPERVISION

Article 15

1. The Regent has the authority to conduct guidance, control and supervision of all activities related to the implementation of prevention, protection and recovery of women and children victims of violence and exploitation in the region.
2. The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) is technically and operationally implemented by the Agency.

heading: Article 16
CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 17

1. The community can participate in efforts to prevent, protect and recover victims of violence against women and children.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) can be carried out by individuals or organizations.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) can be carried out in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against women and children occur;
c. providing assistance to victims of acts of violence against women and children.

heading: CHAPTER IX
CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

SOURCES OF FUNDS

Article 19

1. Expenditure for programs and activities for the Implementation of Prevention, Protection and Recovery of Women and Children as Victims of Acts of Violence is sourced from the Indramayu Regency APBD.
2. In addition to being sourced from the APBD, program and activity expenditure as referred to in paragraph (1) may be sourced from the APBN, Provincial APBD and other legal and non-binding sources.
3. To support the operational expenditure of P2TP2A, a budget sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD) may be provided.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

CRIMINAL SANCTIONS

Article 20

1. Any person who obstructs, disturbs and/or hinders the implementation of programs for the implementation of prevention, protection and recovery of women and children victims of acts of violence, is threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of at most Rp. 50,000,000.00 (Fifty Million Rupiah).
2. In addition to criminal acts as referred to in paragraph (1) whether in the form of criminal violations and/or actions resulting in losses to the Regional Government, individuals or other parties are threatened with criminal law in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XII
CHAPTER XIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 22

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

So that everyone may know, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Indramayu Regency Enacted in Indramayu on 26 December 2012

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF INDRAMAYU REGENCY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF INDRAMAYU REGENCY

NUMBER 18 YEAR 2012 CONCERNING PREVENTION, PROTECTION AND RECOVERY OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AS VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN INDRAMAYU REGENCY

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF INDRAMAYU REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage security, psychological, physical, sexual, and economic well-being. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's territory.

Because the Indonesian government has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning the elimination of all forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to fulfill these provisions. The enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State.

Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the government recognizes the existence of children's rights. Human Rights inherent in children include, among others, basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

To fulfill the right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is provided to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, society and parents are obliged to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (The best Interest of Child) is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature.

Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children experiencing problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of persecution, neglect, eviction and abuse by parents or others. For women and children experiencing such problems, the government must provide a Safe House (Children protection home) or integrated service center for women and children (P2TP2A) for women and children victims of violence. A Safe House (shelter) is a safe place that is Friendly for women and children.

The Integrated Service Center is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, clerics/religious leaders and is networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police.

The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The large number of cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of truth, justice, legal certainty, equality and upholding Human Rights.

From the above framework, the regional government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women. One such effort is the realization of a legal framework in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.

heading: Article 2
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF INDRAMAYU REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 2

What is meant by "Respect for the rights of victims" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims.

What is meant by "Justice and gender equality" is a process to be fair to men and women and equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and National security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.

What is meant by "Non-Discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

What is meant by "The best interests of victims" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by regional government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the primary consideration.

heading: Article 3
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF INDRAMAYU REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 3

Letter a
The "prevention" aspect is a strategic protection effort through:
a. Primary prevention, all people, families, communities and the state in efforts to increase knowledge capacity, understanding and ensure that violence against women and children does not occur, including policy socialization, adequate services, supportive workplace policies, and life skill training for women and children.

What is meant by life skill training includes conflict resolution without violence, stress management skills, resource management, effective decision making, effective interpersonal communication, guidance on psychosocial development of women and children.

b. Secondary prevention, aimed at high-risk community groups in efforts to improve skills, including training and victim services to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur in the next generation. Activities carried out here include home visits for parents who have just had children to conduct self-assessment of whether they are at risk of committing violence against children in the future.
c. Tertiary prevention, intended to improve parenting capacity that ensures violence against women and children does not recur, what is done here is integrated services for women and children who are victims of violence, through counseling, stress management training.

Letter b
The "service and assistance" aspect is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals and assistance in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.

Letter c
The "recovery" aspect is an effort to restore and rehabilitate the physical and psychological condition of victims which then reunites them with the victim's family and community.

Letter d
The "empowerment" aspect is a process of increasing the role of the community to participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence which aims to obtain access and participation in the protection process for women and children broadly.

heading: Article 4
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF INDRAMAYU REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 4

Letter a
What is meant by "receiving protection" is receiving protection from individuals, groups and institutions both governmental and non-governmental.

Letter b
What is meant by "receiving information" is access and information about the existence of complaint centers, PPT, and all matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and involvement in the decision-making process related to assistance and case developments.

Letter c
What is meant by "minimum service" is service that includes medical, extensive medicolegal, psychosocial and legal services.

Letter d
What is meant by "continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage" is handling that does not stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume life in society including the restoration of their good name.

Letter e
What is meant by "confidential handling" is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical care and legal handling will not be disseminated.

Letter f
What is meant by "receiving psychological assistance" is assistance provided by psychologists to victims suffering from trauma/other psychological problems to restore the victim's psychological condition. While legal assistance is assistance provided by persons and/or legal aid institutions to persons at every level of examination and throughout the legal process.

Letter g
What is meant by "guarantee of rights related to victim status" is an effort to provide certainty and protection for victims as family members and community members.

heading: Article 12
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF INDRAMAYU REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 12

Letter a
What is meant by "fast" is immediate action taken without complications or simplified procedures.

What is meant by "safe" is a guarantee of service protection that feels comfortable, undisturbed, and served in a friendly, respectful and appreciative manner.

What is meant by "empathy" is actions of appreciating, respecting, caring, being friendly, and making happy which aim to please and calm the victim's heart.
Letter b
What is meant by "guarantee of confidentiality" is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical care and legal handling will not be disseminated.

Letter c
What is meant by "easily accessible" is the provision of services and assistance for all people regardless of their social status, so that such services are affordable for the underprivileged or relatively sufficient for the privileged.

Letter d
What is meant by "not charged" is that service and assistance activities carried out by PPT are not charged to victims.
